destination.name: Gippsland Lakes
destination.tagline: A web of coastal lakes behind Ninety Mile Beach, made for boating and fishing.
destination.description: The Gippsland Lakes are a network of coastal lakes, marshes and lagoons covering about 354 km2 in East Gippsland. Ninety Mile Beach, just over 151 km long, separates them from Bass Strait, and the lakes drain to the sea through a short man-made canal at Lakes Entrance. People cruise, hire boats and kayaks, and fish from jetties at Paynesville, Lakes Entrance and Metung. The lakes are a Ramsar-listed wetland, home to about 50 rare Burrunan dolphins.

goodToKnow.title: Summer beach patrols
goodToKnow.detail: Eastern Beach at Lakes Entrance is patrolled between Christmas and Australia Day. Swim between the flags.

goodToKnow.title: Summer crowds
goodToKnow.detail: The lakeside tourist towns swell in summer, so book accommodation ahead for December to February.
